provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 5 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: presta -> resta; omnipotens -> omni it potens; affligendo -> aftii endo; alimentis -> alimen tis; iustitiam -> iusti tiam; 1922 Mame text layer damages 1 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): presta quesumus omnipotens -> resta queesumus om p nipotens; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 128, artifact PDF p. 242; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 31448 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Concede, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut hujus sacrificii munus oblatum,
fragilitatem nostram ab omni malo purget semper et muniat. Per Dominum
nostrum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut inter ejus membra numeremur, cujus corpori
communicamus, et sanguini: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
